sections.title: 英语知识运用
sections.directions: Directions: Read the following text. Choose the best word(s) for each numbered blank and mark A, B, C or D on the ANSWER SHEET. (10 points)

blocks.content: Thinner isn't always better. A number of studies have
that normal-weight people are in fact at higher risk of some diseases compared to those who are overweight. And there are health conditions for which being overweight is actually
. For example, heavier women are less likely to develop calcium deficiency than thin women.
, among the elderly, being somewhat overweight is often an
of good health. Of even greater
is the fact that obesity turns out to be very difficult to define. It is often defined
body mass index, or BMI. BMI
body mass divided by the square of height. An adult with a BMI of 18 to 25 is often considered to be normal weight. Between 25 and 30 is overweight. And over 30 is considered obese. Obesity,
, can be divided into moderately obese, severely obese, and very severely obese. While such numerical standards seem
, they are not. Obesity is probably less a matter of weight than body fat. Some people with a high BMI are in fact extremely fit,
others with a low BMI may be in poor
. For example, many collegiate and professional football players
as obese, though their percentage body fat is low. Conversely, someone with a small frame may have high body fat but a
BMI. Today we have a(n)
to label obesity as a disgrace. The overweight are sometimes
in the media with their faces covered. Stereotypes
with obesity include laziness, lack of will power, and lower prospects for success. Teachers, employers, and health professionals have been shown to harbor biases against the obese.
very young children tend to look down on the overweight, and teasing about body build has long been a problem in schools. Negative attitudes toward obesity,
in health concerns, have stimulated a number of anti-obesity
. My own hospital system has banned sugary drinks from its facilities. Many employers have instituted weight loss and fitness initiatives. Michelle Obama has launched a high-visibility campaign
childhood obesity, even claiming that it represents our greatest national security threat.

questions.analysis: concluded 【线索】本句论断与下一句例证一致 空所在句 A number of studies have __(1)__ that normal-weight people are in fact at higher risk of some diseases compared to those who are overweight. 提出一个具体论 断；紧接的 And there are health conditions for which being overweight is actually __(2)__. 与 heavier women are less likely to develop calcium deficiency than thin 【选项】A) denied ✗ 与后文同向例证矛盾 denied 意为"否认"，若研究否认该论断，则下一句不会用 And 引出同向例证 heavier women are less likely to develop calcium deficiency than thin women.，逻辑反向。 B) concluded ✓ 得出结论，与后文例证同向 concluded 意为"得出结论"，与 A number of studies have __(1)__ that normal-weight people are in fact at higher risk of some diseases 这一断言式句式天然契合，并被随后的 calcium deficiency 例证印证。 C) doubted ✗ 存疑态度与例证矛盾 doubted 表"怀疑"，但作者紧接着用 in fact 强调结论的确定性，态度不符。 D) ensured ✗ 搭配与语义双重不当 【验证】代回得 A number of studies have __(1)__ that normal-weight people are in fact at higher risk of some diseases compared to those who are overweight.，与全文第 1

protective 【线索】举例句确认"超重反而有益" 紧随其后的 For example, heavier women are less likely to develop calcium deficiency 护性"。 【选项】 A) protective ✓ 保护性，与例证同向 protective 意为"有保护作用的"，与 heavier women are less likely to develop calcium deficiency than thin women. 完美对应——超重反而保护骨骼。 B) dangerous ✗ 方向与本段反常识脉络相反 C) sufficient ✗ 语义不搭 sufficient"充足的"，不能用来评价 being overweight 对健康的作用方向，搭配不通。 D) troublesome ✗ 带负面色彩，与例证矛盾 【验证】代回得 there are health conditions for which being overweight is actually __(2)__，再 接 For example, heavier women are less likely to develop calcium deficiency than

Likewise 【线索】前后两句都是"超重反而好"的例证 前句 For example, heavier women are less likely to develop calcium deficiency than thin women. 与本句 __(3)__, among the elderly, being somewhat overweight is often an __(4)__ of good health. 都是在"超重在某些情况下反而有益"这条主线下并列举例—— 【选项】A) Instead ✗ 替代关系不成立 B) However ✗ 转折与同向例证矛盾 C) Likewise ✓ 同向类推，最契合并列例证 Likewise"同样地"，把女性缺钙这条例证类推到 among the elderly，两条同方向例证由它衔接 D) Therefore ✗ 本句不是结论而是另一例证 【验证】代回得 Likewise, among the elderly, being somewhat overweight is often an __(4)__

indicator 【线索】老人超重"是"健康的标志 本句 among the elderly, being somewhat overweight is often an __(4)__ of good 【选项】 A) indicator ✓ 指示信号，最契合 indicator"指示物、迹象"与 being somewhat overweight is often an __(4)__ of good health B) objective ✗ 把现象误读成目标 C) origin ✗ 因果关系不对 D) example ✗ 搭配不当 example 常说 example of good health 指"健康的范例"，但主语是"略胖"这一状态而非个体，将 【验证】代回得 among the elderly, being somewhat overweight is often an indicator of good

concern 【线索】下文揭示一个值得关切的事实 本句 Of even greater __(5)__ is the fact that obesity turns out to be very difficult to 【选项】A) impact ✗ 影响维度无对象支撑 impact"影响"需要指明影响对象，但本句的 the fact that obesity turns out to be very difficult B) relevance ✗ 相关性方向偏移 C) assistance ✗ 完全不搭 assistance"帮助"与"肥胖难以定义"无任何关系。 D) concern ✓ 更值得关切，命中作者立场 concern"关切、担忧"与 Of even greater __(5)__ is the fact that obesity turns out to be very difficult to define. 完美对应——"更让人担心的事实是肥胖难以定义"，引出后文对 BMI 的整段 【验证】代回得 Of even greater concern is the fact that obesity turns out to be very difficult

in terms of 【线索】本句框架"用 BMI 来定义" 本句 It is often defined __(6)__ body mass index, or BMI. 框架是"用 X 这一指标来定义 Y"，空处要填"按……来/根据……"。 【选项】 A) in terms of ✓ 按 …… 来衡量，最契合 in terms of"按……来说、依据……来衡量"，与"用 BMI 来定义肥胖"完全对应。 B) in case of ✗ 条件义不通 in case of"万一/以防"，引出条件，与定义无关。 C) in favor of ✗ 支持义不通 in favor of"支持"，与本句"以 BMI 为标准"语义对不上。 D) in respects of ✗ 非规范英语短语 in respects of 不是规范英语短语，规范说法是 in respect of 或 with respect to；考研完形里这 【验证】代回得 It is often defined in terms of body mass index, or BMI.，意为"通常用 BMI 来

equals 【线索】公式义"等于体重除以身高的平方" 本句 BMI __(7)__ body mass divided by the square of height. 是 BMI 的数学定义：BMI 【选项】A) measures ✗ 测量 ≠ 数学等于 measures"测量、衡量"指动作过程，常说"X measures Y in Z"，但本句给的是数学公式，要的是 B) determines ✗ 决定义不等同公式 determines"决定"，B 决定 A 是因果义，与"BMI = …"的纯数学定义不符。 C) equals ✓ 等于，正中公式定义 equals"等于"与 BMI __(7)__ body mass divided by the square of height. 这一公式陈述完全 D) modifies ✗ 修改义离题 modifies"修改、改变"，与公式定义毫无关系。 【验证】代回得 BMI equals body mass divided by the square of height.，作为 BMI 的数学定 义，与下文随即给出的数值区间（18–25、25–30、30+）顺利衔接。

in turn 【线索】上文给"肥胖"门槛，本句再细分肥胖 前句 And over 30 is considered obese. 给出肥胖门槛；本句 Obesity, __(8)__, can be divided into moderately obese, severely obese, and very severely obese. 再把"肥 【选项】A) in essence ✗ 本质归纳与细分不符 B) in contrast ✗ 无对比对象 C) in turn ✓ 依次细分，最契合 in turn"接下来又、依次"与 Obesity, __(8)__, can be divided into moderately obese, severely obese, and very severely obese. 这一从大类到子类的递进细分完全吻合。 D) in part ✗ 部分义不对 【验证】代回得 Obesity, in turn, can be divided into moderately obese, severely obese, and very severely obese.，承接前面 BMI 分档自然递进到肥胖内部再分档，第 2 段"先定义—

straightforward 【线索】While seem ___, they are not 形成对比 本句 While such numerical standards seem __(9)__, they are not. 用 While + seem … they are not 形成"表面 / 实际"的反转——前文 BMI 18–25、25–30、>30 这套数字一望 【选项】A) complicated ✗ 方向相反 B) conservative ✗ 语义不搭 conservative"保守的"，用来形容数值标准不通顺，且无法被 they are not 自然否定。 C) variable ✗ 易变义偏离原意 D) straightforward ✓ 直白明了，最契合 straightforward"简单明了的、直截了当的"，与 While such numerical standards seem __(9)__, they are not. 的"看似清楚但其实不然"完全契合，后文随即解释 BMI 高未必胖、BMI 低 【验证】代回得 While such numerical standards seem straightforward, they are not.，紧接 Obesity is probably less a matter of weight than body fat. 揭示数值标准的局限，整

while 【线索】BMI 高却健身 vs BMI 低却不健康 本句 Some people with a high BMI are in fact extremely fit, __(10)__ others with a low BMI may be in poor __(11)__. 两个分句明显对比："BMI 高—很 fit"和"BMI 低—状态 【选项】A) so ✗ 因果不成立 B) while ✓ 对比连词，最契合 while"而、与此相反"，正好连接 Some people with a high BMI… 与 others with a low BMI… 两端反向例子，与 Some people with a high BMI are in fact extremely fit, __(10)__ others with a low BMI may be in poor __(11)__. 的对比结构吻合。 C) since ✗ 原因关系不对 D) unless ✗ 条件关系不对 【验证】代回得 Some people with a high BMI are in fact extremely fit, while others with a low BMI may be in poor __(11)__.，与前句"数值标准不可靠"的论点保持一致——通过两类反

shape 【线索】fit 与 in poor ___ 形成反义对照 本句前半 Some people with a high BMI are in fact extremely fit 与后半 others with a low BMI may be in poor __(11)__ 反义对照——一组 fit，一组身体状态差。空处要承 【选项】 A) shape ✓ in poor shape，固定搭配 shape 与 in poor 构成固定搭配 in poor shape"身体状态差"，与前半 extremely fit 形成完美反 B) spirit ✗ 精神义偏离 spirit 与 in poor 搭配多指"情绪低落"，与上文谈的 fit（身体状态）不在同一维度。 C) balance ✗ 搭配不通 balance 不与 in poor 构成与"身体健康"对应的固定搭配。 D) taste ✗ in poor taste 是"品味差" taste 与 in poor 搭配是 in poor taste"品味差/不得体"，与身体健康话题无关。 【验证】代回得 others with a low BMI may be in poor shape.，与上半句 extremely fit 形成"身

qualify 【线索】BMI 偏高—被算作肥胖，但体脂率低 本句 many collegiate and professional football players __(12)__ as obese, though their percentage body fat is low. 揭示一种反差：球员按 BMI 被算作肥胖，但其实体脂很 【选项】A) start ✗ 起始义不对 start"开始"暗示动作起点，但 many collegiate and professional football players __(12)__ as B) qualify ✓ 够格被归入，最契合 qualify 与 as + 类别构成 qualify as"够格被算作、被认定为"，正好对应"按 BMI 标准被算作 肥胖"。 C) retire ✗ 退役义离题 D) stay ✗ 停留义不准 【验证】代回得 many collegiate and professional football players qualify as obese, though their percentage body fat is low.，作为"BMI 不可靠"论点的关键例证：球员被 BMI 算作

normal 【线索】Conversely 与前句"BMI 高—体脂低"镜像 前句 many collegiate and professional football players __(12)__ as obese, though their percentage body fat is low."BMI 高—体脂低"；本句 Conversely, someone with a small frame may have high body fat but a __(13)__ BMI."骨架小—体脂高—BMI ___ "。 【选项】A) strange ✗ 评价色彩与镜像不符 奇怪"。 B) changeable ✗ 易变义不对 C) normal ✓ 正常 BMI，与体脂高反差 normal"正常的"与 someone with a small frame may have high body fat but a __(13)__ D) constant ✗ 稳定义偏离 【验证】代回得 Conversely, someone with a small frame may have high body fat but a normal BMI.，与前句 football players qualify as obese, though their percentage body fat is low 完美镜像反转，第 3 段"BMI 与真实健康脱节"论点闭环。

tendency 【线索】后文连给三类污名化现象 本句 Today we have a(n) __(14)__ to label obesity as a disgrace. 后立刻给出 The overweight are sometimes __(15)__ in the media with their faces covered.、 Stereotypes __(16)__ with obesity include laziness, lack of will power, and lower prospects for success.、Teachers, employers, and health professionals have been shown to harbor biases against the obese. 三类普遍现象——说明这是一个时代普遍 【选项】A) option ✗ 选项义偏离普遍倾向 B) reason ✗ 理由义与后文不对应 C) opportunity ✗ 机会义色彩不对 D) tendency ✓ 倾向，与后文普遍现象同向 tendency"倾向"与 Today we have a(n) __(14)__ to label obesity as a disgrace. 完美吻合，并 【验证】代回得 Today we have a(n) tendency to label obesity as a disgrace.，作为第 4 段的总

pictured 【线索】in the media + 遮脸细节 本句 The overweight are sometimes __(15)__ in the media with their faces covered. 出现 in the media 和 with their faces covered，明显指"被媒体拍下并展示画面"。 【选项】A) employed ✗ 雇佣义无关 B) pictured ✓ 被拍下/被描绘，最契合 pictured"被拍下、被呈现"与 in the media with their faces covered 这一视觉细节完全对应 C) imitated ✗ 模仿义离题 D) monitored ✗ 监控义不对 monitored"被监控"暗示被持续跟踪，与 with their faces covered 这种一次性画面呈现不匹配。 【验证】代回得 The overweight are sometimes pictured in the media with their faces

associated 【线索】刻板印象与肥胖被"联系在一起" 本句 Stereotypes __(16)__ with obesity include laziness, lack of will power, and lower prospects for success. 表达的是"被与肥胖联系起来的刻板印象"，主语 Stereotypes 与 obesity 是"关联"关系。 【选项】A) compared ✗ 比较义不对 compared with 是"与……相比"，但本句不是把 stereotypes 拿来与 obesity 作比较，而是说它们 B) combined ✗ 合并义偏离 combined with 多用于两种具体事物合并而成新事物，stereotype 与 obesity 不是这种关系。 C) settled ✗ 了结义无关 settled with"与……了结/达成和解"，与本句话题无关。 D) associated ✓ 与……相关联，最契合 associated with"与……相关联"，正好表达"与肥胖被挂钩的刻板印象"，并能引出后续 laziness, lack of will power, lower prospects for success 三个被挂上去的负面标签。 【验证】代回得 Stereotypes associated with obesity include laziness, lack of will power, and lower prospects for success.，作为第 14 题"污名化倾向"的第二类具体表现——刻板印象

Even 【线索】从成人偏见递进到"连小小孩"也歧视 前句 Teachers, employers, and health professionals have been shown to harbor biases against the obese. 已点出多类成年人都歧视；本句 __(17)__ very young children tend to look down on the overweight 把"很小的孩子也歧视"一并列出，这是程度递进 【选项】 A) Even ✓ 甚至连小孩也歧视，递进 Even"甚至"与 __(17)__ very young children tend to look down on the overweight 完美契 B) Still ✗ 延续/让步力度不够 C) Yet ✗ 转折与同向递进矛盾 D) Only ✗ 限定义反方向 Only very young children tend to… 意味着"只有小孩子才这样"，与前句"老师、雇主、医务人员 【验证】代回得 Even very young children tend to look down on the overweight, and teasing about body build has long been a problem in schools.，与前句"成人偏见普遍"完成"连

grounded 【线索】负面态度有健康考量做基础 本句 Negative attitudes toward obesity, __(18)__ in health concerns, have stimulated a number of anti-obesity __(19)__. 暗示对肥胖的负面态度是"以健康担忧为根据/基础"， 【选项】A) despised ✗ 鄙视义与主语方向不对 B) corrected ✗ 纠正义离题 C) ignored ✗ 忽视义与因果链矛盾 ignored"被忽视的"，但下半句 have stimulated 表明这些态度催生了反肥胖行动，并非被忽视。 D) grounded ✓ 扎根于健康担忧，最契合 grounded in"以……为根据/基础"与 Negative attitudes toward obesity, __(18)__ in health concerns, have stimulated a number of anti-obesity __(19)__. 吻合——这些负面态度根植于 【验证】代回得 Negative attitudes toward obesity, grounded in health concerns, have stimulated a number of anti-obesity __(19)__.，与第 5 段"健康担忧—反肥胖行动"因果

policies 【线索】后文三例都是规则/规定/运动 后文 My own hospital system has banned sugary drinks from its facilities.、Many employers have instituted weight loss and fitness initiatives.、Michelle Obama has launched a high-visibility campaign __(20)__ childhood obesity 都是机构出台的规则/ 计划/运动，统摄词应是"policies/政策措施"。 【选项】A) discussions ✗ 讨论义太弱 B) businesses ✗ 商业义偏离 C) policies ✓ 政策措施，最契合 anti-obesity policies"反肥胖政策"是地道搭配。 D) studies ✗ 研究义不对 studies"研究"是认识层面，但后文举的都是行动层面，且 anti-obesity studies 远不如 anti- obesity policies 自然。 【验证】代回得 have stimulated a number of anti-obesity policies.，作为第 5 段"反肥胖政策"的

against 【线索】上下文"反肥胖政策"定向 本句紧承 have stimulated a number of anti-obesity __(19)__. 给出最知名的一例： Michelle Obama has launched a high-visibility campaign __(20)__ childhood obesity，方向自然是"反对儿童肥胖"；后半 even claiming that it represents our greatest national security threat. 用 threat（威胁）也确认肥胖是被反对的对象。 【选项】A) for ✗ 支持义与反肥胖矛盾 for childhood obesity 意为"为了儿童肥胖"，与整段"反肥胖政策"方向完全相反。 B) against ✓ 反对儿童肥胖，最契合 against childhood obesity"反对儿童肥胖"与上文 anti-obesity 与下文 our greatest national C) with ✗ 伴随义不通 with 与 campaign 搭配常表"借助/伴随"，与本句要表达的方向无关。 D) without ✗ 无……义不通 without"没有"与 campaign 不构成自然搭配，且语义荒谬。 【验证】代回得 Michelle Obama has launched a high-visibility campaign against childhood obesity, even claiming that it represents our greatest national security threat.，与上 文 anti-obesity policies 完全一致，作为最有力的一例收束第 5 段。 OVERVIEW · 通读建境 开篇即给出全篇定调句 Thinner isn't always better.，接着用 normal-weight people are in fact at higher risk of some diseases compared to those who are overweight 把读者熟悉的 probably less a matter of weight than body fat.），再揭示社会对肥胖的偏见与反肥胖运动 （Today we have a(n) __(14)__ to label obesity as a disgrace.）。全文是冷静、略带反思的 第 1 段抛反常识：Thinner isn't always better.；第 2 段把话题切到"如何定义肥胖"并引入 BMI（obesity turns out to be very difficult to define）；第 3 段反转：BMI 数值看似清晰 其实不可靠（While such numerical standards seem __(9)__, they are not.）；第 4 段转向社 会层面，肥胖被贴上 disgrace 标签（Stereotypes __(16)__ with obesity include laziness, lack of will power, and lower prospects for success.）；第 5 段顺势谈反肥胖行动（have stimulated a number of anti-obesity __(19)__）。逐...

sections.title: 阅读理解
sections.directions: Read the following four texts. Answer the questions after each text by choosing A, B, C or D. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (40 points)

blocks.content: What would you do with $590m? This is now a question for Gloria MacKenzie, an 84-year-old widow who recently emerged from her small, tin-roofed house in Florida to collect the biggest undivided lottery jackpot in history. If she hopes her new-found fortune will yield lasting feelings of fulfillment, she could do worse than read Happy Money by Elizabeth Dunn and Michael Norton. These two academics use an array of behavioral research to show that the most rewarding ways to spend money can be counterintuitive. Fantasies of great wealth often involve visions of fancy cars and extravagant homes. Yet satisfaction with these material purchases wears off fairly quickly. What was once exciting and new becomes old-hat; regret creeps in. It is far better to spend money on experiences, say Ms Dunn and Mr Norton, like interesting trips, unique meals or even going to the cinema. These purchases often become more valuable with time – as stories or memories – particularly if they involve feeling more connected to others. This slim volume is packed with tips to help wage slaves as well as lottery winners get the most "happiness bang for your buck." It seems most people would be better off if they could shorten their commutes to work, spend more time with friends and family and less of it watching television (something the average American spends a whopping two months a year doing, and is hardly jollier for it). Buying gifts or giving to charity is often more pleasurable than purchasing things for oneself, and luxuries are most enjoyable when they are consumed sparingly. This is apparently the reason McDonald's restricts the availability of its popular McRib – a marketing trick that has turned the pork sandwich into an object of obsession. Readers of Happy Money are clearly a privileged lot, anxious about fulfilment, not hunger. Money may not quite buy happiness, but people in wealthier countries are generally happier than those in poor ones. Yet the link between feeling good and spending money on others can be seen among rich and poor people around the world, and scarcity enhances the pleasure of most things for most people. Not everyone will agree with the authors' policy ideas, which range from mandating more holiday time to reducing tax incentives for American homebuyers. But most people will come away from this book believing it was money well spent.

An article in Scientific American has pointed out that empirical research says that, actually, you think you're more beautiful than you are. We have a deep-seated need to feel good about ourselves and we naturally employ a number of self-enhancing strategies to achieve this. Social psychologists have amassed oceans of research into what they call the "above average effect", or "illusory superiority", and shown that, for example, 70% of us rate ourselves as above average in leadership, 93% in driving and 85% at getting on well with others – all obviously statistical impossibilities. We rose-tint our memories and put ourselves into self-affirming situations. We become defensive when criticised, and apply negative stereotypes to others to boost our own esteem. We stalk around thinking we're hot stuff. Psychologist and behavioural scientist Nicholas Epley oversaw a key study into self-enhancement and attractiveness. Rather than have people simply rate their beauty compared with others, he asked them to identify an original photograph of themselves from a lineup including versions that had been altered to appear more and less attractive. Visual recognition, reads the study, is "an automatic psychological process, occurring rapidly and intuitively with little or no apparent conscious deliberation". If the subjects quickly chose a falsely flattering image – which most did – they genuinely believed it was really how they looked. Epley found no significant gender difference in responses. Nor was there any evidence that those who self- enhanced the most (that is, the participants who thought the most positively doctored pictures were real) were doing so to make up for profound insecurities. In fact, those who thought that the images higher up the attractiveness scale were real directly corresponded with those who showed other markers for having higher self- esteem. "I don't think the findings that we have are any evidence of personal delusion," says Epley. "It's a reflection simply of people generally thinking well of themselves." If you are depressed, you won't be self- enhancing. Knowing the results of Epley's study, it makes sense that many people hate photographs of themselves viscerally – on one level, they don't even recognise the person in the picture as themselves. Facebook, therefore, is a self-enhancer's paradise, where people can share only the most flattering photos, the cream of their wit, style, beauty, intellect and lifestyles. It's not that people's profiles are dishonest, says Catalina Toma of Wisconsin-Madison University, "but they portray an idealised version of themselves."

The concept of man versus machine is at least as old as the industrial revolution, but this phenomenon tends to be most acutely felt during economic downturns and fragile recoveries. And yet, it would be a mistake to think we are right now simply experiencing the painful side of a boom and bust cycle. Certain jobs have gone away for good, outmoded by machines. Since technology has such an insatiable appetite for eating up human jobs, this phenomenon will continue to restructure our economy in ways we cannot immediately foresee. When there is rapid improvement in the price and performance of technology, jobs that were once thought to be immune from automation suddenly become threatened. This argument has attracted a lot of attention, via the success of the book Race Against the Machine, by Erik Brynjolfsson and Andrew McAfee, who both hail from MIT's Center for Digital Business. This is a powerful argument, and a scary one. And yet, John Hagel, author of The Power of Pull and other books, says Brynjolfsson and McAfee miss the reason why these jobs are so vulnerable to technology in the first place. Hagel says we have designed jobs in the U.S. that tend to be "tightly scripted" and "highly standardized" ones that leave no room for "individual initiative or creativity". In short, these are the types of jobs that machines can perform much better at than human beings. That is how we have put a giant target sign on the backs of American workers, Hagel says. It's time to reinvent the formula for how work is conducted, since we are still relying on a very 20th century notion of work, Hagel says. In our rapidly changing economy, we more than ever need people in the workplace who can take initiative and exercise their imagination "to respond to unexpected events". That is not something machines are good at. They are designed to perform very predictable activities. As Hagel notes, Brynjolfsson and McAfee indeed touched on this point in their book. We need to reframe race against the machine as race with the machine. In other words, we need to look at the ways in which machines can augment human labor rather than replace it. So then the problem is not really about technology, but rather, "how do we innovate our institutions and our work practices?"

When the government talks about infrastructure contributing to the economy the focus is usually on roads, railways, broadband and energy. Housing is seldom mentioned. Why is that? To some extent the housing sector must shoulder the blame. We have not been good at communicating the real value that housing can contribute to economic growth. Then there is the scale of the typical housing project. It is hard to shove for attention among multibillion-pound infrastructure projects, so it is inevitable that the attention is focused elsewhere. But perhaps the most significant reason is that the issue has always been so politically charged. Nevertheless, the affordable housing situation is desperate. Waiting lists increase all the time and we are simply not building enough new homes. The comprehensive spending review offers an opportunity for the government to help rectify this. It needs to put historical prejudices to one side and take some steps to address our urgent housing need. There are some indications that it is preparing to do just that. The communities minister, Don Foster, has hinted that George Osborne, Chancellor of the Exchequer, may introduce more flexibility to the current cap on the amount that local authorities can borrow against their housing stock debt. Evidence shows that 60,000 extra new homes could be built over the next five years if the cap were lifted, increasing GDP by 0.6%. Ministers should also look at creating greater certainty in the rental environment, which would have a significant impact on the ability of registered providers to fund new developments from revenues. But it is not just down to the government. While these measures would be welcome in the short term, we must face up to the fact that the existing £4.5bn programme of grants to fund new affordable housing, set to expire in 2015, is unlikely to be extended beyond then. The Labour party has recently announced that it will retain a large part of the coalition's spending plans if it returns to power. The housing sector needs to accept that we are very unlikely to ever return to the era of large-scale public grants. We need to adjust to this changing climate. While the government's commitment to long-term funding may have changed, the very pressing need for more affordable housing is real and is not going away.

Part B Directions: Read the following text and match each of the numbered items in the left column to its corresponding information in the right column. There are two extra choices in the right column. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (10 points) Emerging in the late Sixties and reaching a peak in the Seventies, Land Art was one of a range of new forms, including Body Art, Performance Art, Action Art and Installation Art, which pushed art beyond the traditional confines of the studio and gallery. Rather than portraying landscape, land artists used the physical substance of the land itself as their medium. The British land art, typified by Richard Long's piece, was not only more domestically scaled, but a lot quirkier than its American counterpart. Indeed, while you might assume that an exhibition of Land Art would consist only of records of works rather than the works themselves, Long's photograph of his work is the work. Since his "action" is in the past, the photograph is its sole embodiment. That might seem rather an obscure point, but it sets the tone for an exhibition that contains a lot of black- and-white photographs and relatively few natural objects. Long is Britain's best-known Land Artist and his Stone Circle, a perfect ring of purplish rocks from Portishead beach laid out on the gallery floor, represents the elegant, rarefied side of the form. The Boyle Family, on the other hand, stand for its dirty, urban aspect. Comprising artists Mark Boyle and Joan Hills and their children, they recreated random sections of the British landscape on gallery walls. Their Olaf Street Study, a square of brick-strewn waste ground, is one of the few works here to embrace the commonplaceness that characterises most of our experience of the landscape most of the time. Parks feature, particularly in the earlier works, such as John Hilliard's very funny Across the Park, in which a long-haired stroller is variously smiled at by a pretty girl and unwittingly assaulted in a sequence of images that turn out to be different parts of the same photograph. Generally however British land artists preferred to get away from towns, gravitating towards landscapes that are traditionally considered beautiful such as the Lake District or the Wiltshire Downs. While it probably wasn't apparent at the time, much of this work is permeated by a spirit of romantic escapism that the likes of Wordsworth would have readily understood. Derek Jarman's yellow-tinted film Towards Avebury, a collection of long, mostly still shots of the Wiltshire landscape, evokes a tradition of English landscape painting stretching from Samuel Palmer to Paul Nash. In the case of Hamish Fulton, you can't help feeling that the Scottish artist has simply found a way of making his love of walking pay. A typical work, such as Seven Days, consists of a single beautiful black-and- white photograph taken on an epic walk, with the mileage and number of days taken listed beneath. British Land Art as shown in this well selected, but relatively modestly scaled exhibition wasn't about imposing on the landscape, more a kind of landscape-orientated light conceptual art created passing through. It had its origins in the great outdoors, but the results were as gallery-bound as the paintings of Turner and Constable. took.
